words.defn_en: to enter a place, situation, or private matter without invitation or permission:
words.root_note: in- (into or upon) + trude (to thrust or push)

sentences.en: Paparazzi continued to ______ upon the celebrity's private vacation by hiding nearby with cameras.
sentences.zh: 狗仔隊躲在附近使用相機，持續侵擾這位名人的私人假期。

sentences.en: The scientist warned that the highway would ______ into protected wetlands and disturb nesting birds.
sentences.zh: 科學家警告，公路將侵入受保護濕地並干擾鳥類築巢。

words.defn_en: to force an unwanted idea, opinion, or presence into a situation or into people's notice:
words.defn_zh: 強加；硬推入；強行干擾；闖入
words.root_note: ob- (against or in the way) + trude (to thrust or push)

sentences.en: The consultant tended to ______ her political opinions into corporate meetings where they did not belong.
sentences.zh: 這位顧問常把不合時宜的個人政治觀點強加到公司會議中。

sentences.en: A noisy protest began to ______ upon the silence of the memorial service.
sentences.zh: 嘈雜的抗議開始闖入追悼會的寂靜，迫使演講者暫停。

words.defn_en: noticeable in an unpleasant, distracting, or unwanted way:
words.defn_zh: 過分顯眼的；刺眼的；突兀的；惹人注意的
words.root_note: ob- (against or in the way) + trus (to thrust) + -ive (tending to)

sentences.en: The historic district prohibits ______ neon signs that would ruin its nineteenth-century appearance.
sentences.zh: 歷史街區禁止安裝會破壞十九世紀景觀的刺眼霓虹招牌。

sentences.en: The filmmaker used hidden microphones so her presence would not be ______.
sentences.zh: 紀錄片導演使用隱藏式麥克風，使自己的存在不會顯得突兀。

words.defn_en: not attracting attention or causing disturbance; discreet and subtle:
words.defn_zh: 不引人注意的；低調的；不唐突的

sentences.en: The hotel prides itself on ______ service that never interrupts guests' privacy.
sentences.zh: 這家飯店以低調細緻、不打擾客人隱私的服務自豪。

sentences.en: Stagehands wore black and moved props in an ______ manner during the live performance.
sentences.zh: 舞台工作人員穿著黑衣，在現場演出中以不引人注意的方式移動道具。

words.defn_en: to stick out or extend beyond a surface or boundary:
words.root_note: pro- (forward or out) + trude (to thrust or push)

sentences.en: A sharp fragment of bone had begun to ______ through the patient's torn skin.
sentences.zh: 一塊尖銳骨頭碎片開始從患者撕裂的皮膚中突出。

sentences.en: Jagged stone columns ______ from the ocean floor where volcanoes once erupted.
sentences.zh: 鋸齒狀石柱從海床凸出，所在位置曾發生海底火山爆發。

words.defn_en: difficult to understand because it is complex, obscure, or highly theoretical:
words.defn_zh: 深奧難懂的；晦澀的；玄奧的
words.root_note: ab- (away or hidden from) + trus (to thrust or push)

sentences.en: The textbook contained such ______ equations that even advanced students struggled with them.
sentences.zh: 教科書充滿深奧難懂的方程式，連高年級學生都難以理解。

sentences.en: The lecturer debated an ______ philosophical theory with little relevance to daily life.
sentences.zh: 講者花時間辯論一套與日常生活關聯甚少的玄奧哲學理論。

words.defn_en: to force or press a material out through a small opening or shaped opening:

sentences.en: The factory uses a mechanical press to ______ molten plastic through a shaped nozzle.
sentences.zh: 工廠使用機械壓力機，將熔融塑膠從成形噴嘴擠出。

sentences.en: The children used plastic syringes to ______ colorful clay onto their canvas designs.
sentences.zh: 孩子使用塑膠注射器，把彩色黏土擠到畫布圖案上。

words.defn_en: to gradually enter, take over, or limit another person's land, rights, time, or space:
words.defn_zh: 侵犯；侵佔；蠶食；逐步侵入
words.root_note: Old French encrochier (to seize or catch with a hook)

sentences.en: Attorneys argued that the tracking software would ______ upon citizens' right to privacy.
sentences.zh: 律師主張，追蹤軟體會侵犯公民的隱私權。

sentences.en: Housing developments continue to ______ upon wildlife habitats as the city expands.
sentences.zh: 城市擴張時，住宅開發持續侵佔野生動物棲息地。

words.defn_en: expressing beliefs as unquestionably true and refusing to consider other opinions or evidence:
words.defn_zh: 教條主義的；武斷的；固執己見的
words.root_note: Greek dogma (an opinion or tenet treated as absolute truth)

sentences.en: The professor's ______ teaching style alienated students because he rejected all debate.
sentences.zh: 教授教條式的教學風格疏遠學生，因為他拒絕一切辯論。

sentences.en: People with ______ views often ignore evidence that contradicts their ideology.
sentences.zh: 抱持武斷觀點的人常忽視與自身意識形態矛盾的證據。

words.defn_en: to force someone to act or to make an action necessary through strong pressure:
words.root_note: com- (together or thoroughly) + pellere (to drive or push)

sentences.en: The contract can legally ______ the supplier to deliver the missing parts within forty-eight hours.
sentences.zh: 合約可依法迫使供應商在四十八小時內交付缺少的零件。

sentences.en: The forensic evidence was strong enough to ______ the jury to return a guilty verdict.
sentences.zh: 法醫證據強而有力，足以迫使陪審團作出有罪判決。

words.defn_en: confidently expressing one's needs, opinions, or rights without being aggressive:
words.defn_zh: 堅定自信的；果斷的；勇於表達的
words.root_note: ad- (to) + serere (to join or bind), through Latin asserere (to claim)

sentences.en: Leadership training teaches managers to be ______ rather than aggressive when setting goals.
sentences.zh: 領導力培訓教導經理設定目標時要堅定自信，而非具有攻擊性。

sentences.en: The engineer gave an ______ presentation showing how her innovations saved the company money.
sentences.zh: 工程師進行一場果斷自信的簡報，說明她的創新如何替公司省錢。

words.defn_en: to drive, urge, or strongly motivate someone to take action:
words.root_note: im- (into or forward) + pellere (to drive or push)

sentences.en: Moral conviction served to ______ the philanthropist to fund free medical clinics.
sentences.zh: 道德信念促使慈善家資助免費醫療診所。

sentences.en: Panic began to ______ passengers toward the lifeboats when alarms sounded on the sinking ship.
sentences.zh: 沉船警報響起時，恐慌驅使乘客湧向救生艇。
